title: Residual diagnostics and the assumptions of regression

videos.script: A regression always produces an answer. Give it any two columns and it returns a slope, an intercept, an R squared and a p-value, whether the data suits a straight line or not. {{answer}} So the last step of every regression is to check it, and the place to look is what the model left behind: the residuals. {{residuals}} If the model has captured the pattern in the data, the residuals are just noise. A shapeless band around zero. {{band}} If they show a shape, the shape is a message. A curve means the relationship is not straight. A funnel means the noise grows as the predictions grow. Runs of positive and negative residuals mean the observations are not independent, often because something that changes over time is missing from the model. {{shapes}} And sometimes the message is a single point: one delivery whose position gives it the power to pull the whole line towards it. {{point}} This lesson reads residual plots, names the four assumptions behind a regression's p-values and intervals, and says what to do when one of them fails. {{fails}}
